headline: An energy-supply shock on top of 5% long yields
analysis: Three things dominate this page: WTI spot 81% above where the year started, a 10-year yield of about 5% against US CPI inflation that has re-accelerated to 3.7%, and a record 65 armed conflicts. They are linked in the data, but loosely. Oil moves with yields and against stocks, gold has followed yields rather than conflict, and equities held up until a tech-led sell-off on 30 Oct took the S&P 500 3.1% below its record close.
evidence: Scorecard; headline tiles; conflict cards; news panel

headline: Oil is the transmission channel
analysis: WTI averaged 58.0 in December 2025, 91.4 in March and 102.1 in May, dipped to 80.5 in July and was back at 97.3 in September; October's EIA average so far is 101.4. On 30 Oct WTI settled at 104.12, up 15.2% on the month and its fourth monthly gain in a row. Brent's expiring December contract settled at 117.64, up 13.6% on the month and its highest since 29 April, and the January contract that is now the front month settled at 113.43, so the roll alone lowers the quoted Brent by 4.21. The EIA spot spread between dated Brent and WTI was 19.73 dollars on 27 Oct (Brent 123.10, WTI 103.37; FRED confirms the Brent figure), wider than on 99% of days since 2016 (median 3.96): the physical market is paying about 9 dollars more than the December futures. Oil fell about 3% on Monday 2 Nov, with Brent near 110 and WTI near 100.7, as US-Iran talks mediated by Qatar raised hopes of reopening the Strait of Hormuz after limpet-mine attacks on a tanker on 30 Oct. That pattern fits a supply-risk premium on seaborne crude tied to the war that began in February; I have not tested causation.
evidence: Oil chart; Brent minus WTI chart; scorecard; news panel

headline: Oil and yields move together, but only loosely
analysis: The correlation of monthly changes is +0.31 over 60 months and +0.40 over the last 12, so oil explains roughly 10% to 16% of yield moves. Oil this month barely predicts next month's yield change (+0.17), so the link is coincident, not a lead. US CPI inflation fell from 4.25% in May to 3.4% in August, then jumped to 3.74% in September as the 16% rise in the September oil average fed through, which is the risk I had flagged. The Fed's preferred gauge, PCE, rose 3.6% year on year in September (Yahoo Finance).
evidence: Correlation table; rolling correlation; CPI chart

headline: Stocks look more oil-sensitive lately
analysis: The oil and S&P 500 correlation moved from -0.14 over 60 months to -0.44 over the last 12 (24-month: -0.13). That is only 12 observations, so read it as a direction. The S&P 500 then fell 1.82% on 30 Oct, its worst day since 5 June, to 7,580.07, which is 3.05% below its 6 Oct record close of 7,818.93, as Amazon and Intel earnings renewed worries about AI spending. The Nasdaq lost 5.3% in October, its worst month since March 2025, while the Dow gained 1.7%. The VIX closed at 19.42, inside its 52-week range of 13.38 to 35.30, after trading as high as 23.93 that day.
evidence: Correlation table; S&P and VIX charts; news panel

headline: Gold has traded as a rates asset, not a conflict hedge
analysis: Gold's correlation with the 10-year yield is -0.29 over 60 months and -0.40 over 12, against 0.00 and -0.09 with oil and +0.14 and +0.11 with stocks. Spot gold is 20.0% below its Q1 2026 average (2 Nov) despite record conflict. The dollar is up against EUR (3.7%), JPY (2.7%) and INR (8.1%) over a year but flat to GBP (-0.4%) and down against CNY (-6.3%), so I would not lean on a dollar explanation.
evidence: Correlation table; gold charts; FX card

headline: Industrial-leaning metals are falling harder than gold
analysis: Against Q1 2026 averages, silver is down 40.2%, platinum 35.1% and gold 20.0%; palladium is down 21.9% since 27 Sep. The gold to silver ratio rose from 58.0 in Q1 2026 to 77.6. That is consistent with weaker industrial demand or a positioning unwind in silver; the data cannot separate the two.
evidence: Metals charts; gold to silver ratio

headline: Real yields are firm, the curve is not inverted
analysis: The market's own real 10-year yield, from inflation-protected Treasuries, was 2.63% on 29 Oct, with a 10-year breakeven inflation rate of 2.35% (Fed H.15). That is well above my rough CPI-based proxy (1.29 points in September on the dashboard's real-yield chart) because the market expects inflation to fall from today's 3.7%; the Fed's effective policy rate is 3.88%. The 10-year auction yield rose from 4.580% in July to 5.300% in October (+72 basis points), and the 26 Oct 2-year auction covered 2.59 times against an average of 2.64. The 27 Oct 5-year auction cleared at 4.845% with a cover of 2.33, and the 29 Oct 7-year at 4.894% with a cover of 2.46 against an average of 2.49, which is in line (coupon 4.875%). With the 10-year 0.38 points above the 2-year (Treasury, 30 Oct), the curve points to inflation and term-premium pressure rather than imminent recession. The Fed held at 3.75% to 4.00% on 28 Oct with two members voting for a hike, after raising rates last month, and traders expect tightening to resume in December (Bloomberg).
evidence: Real yield chart; yield curve; auction table and trend

headline: Conflict intensity and market relevance differ
analysis: There are 65 state-based conflicts, a record, including 8 interstate (4 in 2024) and 14 in the Middle East, also a record. Europe has one conflict (Ukraine) but 61.7% of battle deaths. Markets are reacting to the Middle East, not to Europe's deadliest war, plausibly because of the oil chokepoints involved. That is a hypothesis; the dashboard shows the pieces, not a tested link.
evidence: Conflict cards; conflict intensity table; oil charts

headline: A record clean build alongside an oil spike
analysis: Solar added 511.2 GW and wind 158.7 GW in 2025, the largest annual additions in the series. Oil above 100 dollars improves the relative economics of renewables, but nothing here measures power prices, so treat the link as a hypothesis.

headline: Climate and nuclear risks are not in the market data
analysis: CO2 was 2.07 ppm higher than a year earlier in August and the 12-month mean temperature anomaly is 1.04 C. FAS estimates 12,187 nuclear warheads, with military stockpiles rising again, and describes New START as now expired. None of these shows up in the price series, and I found no short-term link.

headline: Near-term triggers
analysis: The US midterm elections on 3 Nov and the Treasury's refunding announcement on 4 Nov; the Doha talks on reopening Hormuz and whether tanker attacks continue; OPEC+'s next meeting on 29 Nov; Brent's roll to the January contract, which already lowers the quoted price by about 4 dollars; the December Fed meeting, where a hike is expected; whether the 10-year stays below 5%; and whether the tech sell-off spreads. A break in the gold and yield relationship would also change the read on gold.

headline: Limits of the evidence
analysis: The correlations use monthly changes over 60 and 12 observations and do not prove causes. The EIA spot series ends 27 Oct while the tiles and oil chart use futures. Metals daily data comes from an aggregator. Several series have a single source (see Data quality). I have not seen the dashboard render.
